Package org.cibseven.bpm.engine.runtime

Interface AdHocSubProcessActivationBuilder

All Known Implementing Classes:
AdHocSubProcessActivationBuilderImpl
public interface AdHocSubProcessActivationBuilder
Starts activities of an ad hoc sub process, with variables belonging to each performance.

The specification allows an activity to be performed more than once, and the two performances are not obliged to be given the same arguments. That is what this builder expresses and what RuntimeService#activateAdHocSubProcessActivities(String, java.util.Collection, Map) cannot: there the variables are keyed by activity id, so naming one activity twice in a single call leaves one entry in the map and both performances take it. 

 runtimeService.createAdHocSubProcessActivation(scopeExecutionId)
     .startActivity("search").setVariable("query", "invoices 2026")
     .startActivity("search").setVariable("query", "credit notes 2026")
     .execute();

Variables set after a startActivity belong to that performance. They are local to the activity that is started, as they are for the older method.

Everything else is unchanged: the call is all-or-nothing, so one unstartable id starts none of the others, and it returns the activity instance id of each performance in the order requested.

  • Method Details

    • startActivity

      AdHocSubProcessActivationBuilder startActivity(String activityId)
      Adds a performance of the activity with the given id. Naming the same activity twice performs it twice, which the specification explicitly permits.

    • setVariable

      AdHocSubProcessActivationBuilder setVariable(String name, Object value)
      Sets one variable on the performance added last.
      Throws:
      BadUserRequestException - if no activity has been named yet

    • setVariables

      AdHocSubProcessActivationBuilder setVariables(Map<String,Object> variables)
      Sets several variables on the performance added last. Null is ignored, so a caller can pass a map it did not build itself without checking.
      Throws:
      BadUserRequestException - if no activity has been named yet

    • execute

      List<String> execute()
      Starts everything named, and returns the activity instance id of each performance in the order it was named.

      An id is null when the performance has not entered an activity instance in this transaction, which is what an activity marked camunda:asyncBefore does: a job exists, an activity instance does not yet.
